steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease a 24-cup mini muffin tin.

Make the muffins: Mix sugar, margarine, and nutmeg together in a large bowl. Stir in milk, then mix in flour and baking powder until just combined. Spoon batter into the prepared muffin cups, filling each 1/2 full.
Bake in the preheated oven until the tops are light golden brown, 15 to 20 minutes. Remove from the oven and transfer to a wire rack.
Immediately place melted margarine in a bowl, and mix sugar and cinnamon together in another bowl.
Dip the top of each warm muffin in melted margarine, then dip in sugar mixture to coat. Let cool for 10 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Donut Muffins
raw_recipe.description: These quick and easy donut muffins are simple to make in a mini muffin pan. They taste just like cinnamon-sugar doughnut holes with a hint of nutmeg.

review.reviewBody: I'm curious about a couple of things about this recipe. First, why did I end up with 24, not 12, of these mini muffins as the recipe indicates? Could it be an AR misprint? Mine is a standard, mini-muffin tin. Second, I really don't like nutmeg much. So WHY do I LOVE these muffins?! And why can't I stop popping them in my mouth? Don't kid yourself by thinking that because they're small you won't eat as much. You'll just eat more of them. And making them in the mini muffin tins was GENIUS, Dianne! That way you get more of that buttery, cinnamony sweetness in every bite! I did make a couple of modifications, but nothing that would significantly alter the recipe. I used butter instead of margarine and, because I have an entire quart of buttermilk to use, I subbed buttermilk for the milk. This worked beautifully, but please note that if you do that you MUST add 1/2 tsp. baking soda and eliminate the baking powder to adjust the acidity and make them rise properly! Plus they're so darned pretty I could just eat them up! (And I already did, with five of them) Your recipe is a beauty, Dianne! ~A hopefully helpful update: because of my curiosity I did some shopping around to learn that the sizes of mini-muffin tins varies, sometimes significantly! This explains the variance in yield with this recipe, to anywhere from 12 to 24 of these little muffins.

I'm the submitter of this recipe and I'd like to add a few notes! First, the recipe should read "butter or margarine." Either one works great. Second, I finally found out from my mom, who got the recipe from my grandma, that this recipe makes 24 mini muffins. You fill the muffins cups 1/2 full with batter, and they should rise to just above top of the muffin tin. You can certainly also make 12 larger mini muffins if you wish, but "officially" this recipe makes 24. I think 12 has worked for me because my muffin tin is on the bigger side. Sorry about the confusion!

These were pretty good, I'm not sure I can rave about them. There was too much cinnamon and sugar on the outside of the muffins, I can't believe I just wrote that! Next time I make these I will try using confectioners' sugar and cinnamon and skip the extra butter, rolling them while still warm should get enough to stick. I liked the flavor of the muffin, cut back a bit on the nutmeg. I definitely will make them again.

I made them & they turned out AWESOME but only because I made the following changes. First, with such a sweet baked product like this, you gotta have some salt for balance: 1/2 a tsp to the muffin batter is perfect. Second in a recipe such as this where you "mix until just combined" (overmixing really messes things up), always separately mix your dry ingredients and then SIFT them into the wet. They omit these steps in the recipe which is a big mistake unless you like uneven clumps of baking powder. Other than that everything else was fine. In the batter, I decreased the nutmeg to 1/2tsp & added 3/4tsp cinnamon & felt the spices were perfectly balanced :)

The first time I made these I did the recipe as calls. It was way to much nutmeg. (btw, nutmeg can make you sick) And I got a headache after eating them. And the nutmeg was overpowering This time around I reduced the nutmeg to 1/4 teaspoon and added 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon and 1/4 teaspoon vanilla extract to the recipe. Also, I cooked them only 15 mins. THEY WERE DELICIOUS! My husband loved them... and so did my kids. Will make again

Super-simple and very good! Two items that I need to watch for next time, though. I used non-stick mini-muffin pans, and I can either lower the temp and/or shorten the cook time. The lower part of the muffins came out rather browned. They should have been more moist than what I did on the first pan. On the 2nd pan, they came out lighter, as I baked for 13 minutes at 375. That's the beauty of recipes - make it your own by tweaking it a bit!

Loved this recipe, but as others recommended, I reduced the nutmeg to 1/4 tsp and substituted cinnamon for the 1/2 tsp.
Also, I found filling mini muffin cups to 3/4 full gave more substantial muffins. Delicious!
Pleasantly, VERY surprised! Doubled the recipe to make 12 regular sized muffins. Used the same baking temperature & time. WOW! The middle is so soft and moist. It’s really is an airy donut muffin!

I love this recipe! And because I love warm spices, I add 1/4tsp each of ground cloves and allspice to the batter. My husbands works at a jail and took a batch in there and everyone loved these little guys. I work security for a factory and took a batch in for some workers, and I have been begged to make these every day! They are a hit! Love These!
So delicious and so easy. I’ve made the original recipe many times but switched it up for the holidays by substituting pumpkin pie spice for the nutmeg and adding a 1/2 cup pumpkin purée.

As suggested in previous posts, I reduced the nutmeg. I also only coated the tops of the muffins. I was making these to share at coffee time and one of the ladies is gluten free so I used a measure for measure gluten free flour. I have to say they turned out pretty good!
These are so easy to make, taste great, and everyone loves them!
These taste like the doughnuts that we used to get at the state fair, yummy!

My very picky grandchildren loved these. *** I would add vanilla extract and maybe zest some lemon or orange into the batter. Much like the chocolate chip muffins, this was kind of flat. Good, but missing something.
Will definitely be making these little gems again.
I made these with my 6 year old grandson. He doesn't like cinnamon and loves powdered sugar doughnuts so we left out the cinnamon and powdered sugar. He lives them!
LOVE this recipe!! The donut muffins taste exactly like donut holes. My husband says they remind him of the tate of a funnel cake.
These were so good, I cut the nutmeg down to 1/4 tsp and used vanilla almond milk. I baked them in a donut hole pan. I will be trying again with different spices.

This recipe was surprisingly good! I overbaked it slightly, and they became dry so if you make it be sure to watch the oven carefully because the sides will start to brown but not the tops. I didn't have nutmeg so I used 1/2 tsp of cinnamon and 2 crushed cloves (the flavor was fantastic.) I recommend this recipe but keep and eye on the oven, my final result was a bit hard.
I personally don't like nutmeg, so I would switch out the nutmeg for cinnamon next time. I also used butter instead of margarine.
